closest_prior_art.citation: MRI-based prediction of PET-defined amyloid status (PubMed 40579043 / AJNR 2025)
closest_prior_art.key_differences: Used standard classical features / small 2D-3D CNNs without 3D foundation model global transfer, lacked residual gated fusion with frozen baseline, had no scanner representation probe, and provided point predictions without conformal ambiguity sets.

dimensions.d2: Locked local 128³ ResNet-34 representation on identical subject-level splits
dimensions.d3: PET-free inference for PET-defined continuous/binary amyloid status
dimensions.d5: Ambiguity-aware calibrated abstention (Conformal prediction sets: {Aβ-}, {Aβ+}, {Aβ-, Aβ+})

fulltext_review_wave_20260822.closest_prior_art_20260822_review: s30 (peer-reviewed, full-text reviewed): PET-free Aβ/tau inference via multimodal AI fusion, Aβ AUROC 0.79 on external ADNI/HABS/NACC test, ComBat harmonization (d3+d4) — but no foundation-model global embedding branch (d1), no locked local CNN on identical splits (d2), no ambiguity-aware conformal abstention (d5). s19 (AJNR A8899, title/abstract screened) remains the closest T1-only comparator. Neither reaches the five-component combination.
fulltext_review_wave_20260822.note: Per-source overlap statements live in evidence_registry_v3 design_impact fields. No reviewed source exhibits the simultaneous five-component CAFT overlap; prior_art_exact_match_found stays false. Claim ceiling remains NOVELTY_CANDIDATE.

research_gap_statement: Investigation of whether the global volumetric representations of a 3D self-supervised brain MRI foundation model (BrainIAC SimCLR-ViT-B), when combined with local 128³ representations from a locked CNN baseline on identical subject-level folds, provide incremental predictive value for PET-defined amyloid status without PET exposure at inference, while explicitly auditing scanner/cohort confounding and providing calibrated ambiguity-aware abstention.

rows.distinction_from_caft: ADLIP is a vision-language model for AD/MCI/CN, not PET-defined amyloid. It uses 3D T1 MRI plus structured clinical text (MMSE, APOE, CSF Abeta/tau, FAQ). HABS-HD zero-shot accuracy was 0.64 (95% CI 0.60-0.67). Outside Method X and not the five-component CAFT combination.
rows.title: A vision-language foundation model for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis using MRI and clinical data

rows.distinction_from_caft: MCI-to-AD conversion, not PET-defined amyloid. Single-timepoint ResNet3D c-index about 0.70; longitudinal CNN+LSTM 0.80-0.90; time-window AUC > 0.85. Relevant to a future R2 survival branch, not to the current CAFT residual gate.
rows.title: Longitudinal structural MRI-based deep learning and radiomics features for predicting Alzheimer's disease progression

rows.distinction_from_caft: 3D CNN AD vs CN accuracy stayed stable after intensity binarization; models used skull-strip contours (Clever Hans). Direct justification for the R1a mask-edge gate before trusting BrainIAC embeddings.
rows.title: Skull-stripping induces shortcut learning in MRI-based Alzheimer's disease classification

rows.distinction_from_caft: A future orthogonal branch that could reduce MRI-amyloid ambiguity.
rows.title: Plasma p-tau217 as a standalone biomarker

rows.distinction_from_caft: ShareGAN synthesizes 3D amyloid PET from structural MRI (SSIM about 0.90; PET+/- accuracy 88.5% and 89.4% on two external sets). PET is the training target, so this is synthesis rather than PET-free Method X inference and is not CAFT.
rows.title: MRI-to-PET synthesis via deep learning for amyloid-beta quantification in Alzheimer's disease

rows.distinction_from_caft: Uses amyloid-PET during pretraining (RCMD) and reports CN/AD and CN/MCI endpoints (relative +6.2% / +7.0% vs missing-modality baselines). Not Method X (PET enters training) and not the five-component CAFT residual gate.
rows.title: BrainAnytime: Anatomy-Aware Cross-Modal Pretraining for Brain Image Analysis with Arbitrary Modality Availability

rows.distinction_from_caft: Strongest available comparator: same endpoint, and it includes A4. 4056 development plus 149 external exams. T1-only AUC 0.61, T1+FLAIR 0.67 internal, 0.65 external, MCI subgroup 0.71. This is the realistic performance envelope for the Method X endpoint and it uses A4, so the CAFT gap claim must be stated against it, not against ADNI-only numbers. PubMed 40579043 is the same article; s02 was merged rather than double-counted.
rows.title: Deep learning-based prediction of PET amyloid status using MRI: multicontrast EfficientNet with independent external validation

rows.distinction_from_caft: CSF Abeta cutoff 980 pg/ml; multimodal accuracy 0.762 +/- 0.04 with guided-backprop XAI. Requires sMRI+rs-fMRI+dMRI, so it is outside the T1-only Method X contract. Scope comparator only; does not implement CAFT.
rows.title: Multimodal MRI accurately identifies amyloid status in unbalanced cohorts in Alzheimer's disease continuum

rows.distinction_from_caft: PMID 41489091 is this JMRI paper, not a separate scanner-manufacturer classification article; s22 was merged rather than double-counted. 1143 ADNI3 subjects (GE/Philips/Siemens). HACA3 beat ComBat on contrast consistency; T2-FLAIR remained hard. Harmonization is still judged by image similarity, not by whether vendor identity stays linearly decodable from embeddings. Strengthens novelty component c4. PMC XML/PDF fetch returned empty, so screening_stage stays TITLE_ABSTRACT_SCREENED.
rows.title: Evaluation of image-level harmonization methods for multi-center MR neuroimaging

rows.distinction_from_caft: Patient distribution shift violates the exchangeability assumption behind split conformal and degrades coverage. Means the conformal coverage this project reports must be presented as an internal marginal guarantee on the calibration distribution, not a transportable one.
rows.title: Making conformal predictors robust in healthcare settings under patient distribution shift

rows.distinction_from_caft: SSL pretraining can look strong internally and fail under realistic shift; supports not assuming BrainIAC embeddings are automatically useful.
rows.title: A cautionary tale of self-supervised learning for brain MRI foundation models

rows.distinction_from_caft: Head-to-head foundation-model comparison; no single backbone wins every task, consistent with FOMO25.
rows.title: A benchmark of MRI foundation models

rows.distinction_from_caft: Directly motivates mask-edge and skull-strip shortcut tests before trusting BrainIAC embeddings.
rows.title: Do 3D medical foundation models see through shortcuts?

rows.distinction_from_caft: Modality-invariant MRI FMs are a neighbouring design; they do not implement CAFT residual gating on PET-defined amyloid.
rows.title: Large-scale modality-invariant foundation models for brain MRI

rows.distinction_from_caft: Supports treating 128-to-96 geometry as a documented domain shift rather than a silent resample.
rows.title: How much MRI preprocessing is enough?

rows.distinction_from_caft: Multimodal fusion is useful for AD biomarkers, but it is not PET-free Method X and not the five-component CAFT gap.
rows.title: AI-driven fusion of multimodal data for Alzheimer's disease biomarker assessment

rows.distinction_from_caft: Generalisation under site shift is a neighbouring concern to the scanner probe; it does not implement residual gated fusion with a locked 128-cubed CNN.
rows.title: Towards generalisable foundation models for neuroimaging

rows.distinction_from_caft: Another 3D SSL encoder family; neighbouring to BrainIAC, not an exact CAFT match.
rows.title: A generalizable 3D framework and model for self-supervised MRI representation learning
